name: Côte d'Ivoire
summary_text: Côte d'Ivoire is dangerous for trans visitors — a sharp recent deterioration. Long considered West Africa's tolerant outlier (same-sex conduct has never been criminalised), the country saw a wave of violence in late 2024: social-media influencers exhorted followers to “hunt” gay and gender-nonconforming people, and dozens of assaults and beatings followed (NYT, Oct 2024). There is no legal gender recognition and no anti-discrimination protection; police response to the hunt wave was inadequate. For a visitor: no statutory exposure, but the 2024 hunt-down campaign makes visible gender nonconformity dangerous, especially in Abidjan.

sources.claim_summary: NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 403); the underlying NYT article (Oct 2024) covers the situation of LGBTQ people in Ivory Coast (Côte d'Ivoire).

UNDP report (Dec 2024) 'African Commission Resolution 275: Ten Years of Advancing LGBT+ Rights in Africa' - includes a Côte d'Ivoire country overview assessing the protective legal environment, investigation/prosecution of perpetrators, access to justice, civic space, and inclusion of LGBT+ people.

sources.title: Côte d'Ivoire - United States Department of State
sources.claim_summary: US State Department 2023 Human Rights Report for Côte d'Ivoire: official assessment including the SOGI section - same-sex conduct not criminalised but societal discrimination, and the significant violence against LGBT persons documented in the report period.

US State Department 2011 Human Rights Report for Côte d'Ivoire: post-electoral-crisis context (3,000 deaths, sexual violence, displacement) - general human-rights baseline with limited LGBT-specific content.

sources.title: Violence, Exclusion and Resilience among Ivoirian Travestis - PMC
sources.claim_summary: Academic article (Critical African Studies, 2015) by Matthew Thomann and Robbie Corey-Boulet: 'Violence, Exclusion and Resilience among Ivoirian Travestis' - travestis (people born male living as women full- or part-time) in Côte d'Ivoire encounter harsher stigmatisation than other sexual/gender minorities; documents violence, exclusion and community resilience.

sources.title: Violence, Exclusion and Resilience among Ivoirian Travestis - PMC
sources.claim_summary: Same article as above (PMC canonical URL): 'Violence, Exclusion and Resilience among Ivoirian Travestis' - the key academic source on trans-feminine people's experiences in Côte d'Ivoire.
